```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, error = FALSE

library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
```

# Model and source

Li 2025 reports the exposure-response (E-R) analysis that supported 5.6 mg/kg
every 3 weeks (Q3W) as the recommended dose of patritumab deruxtecan
(HER3-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate of an anti-HER3 antibody and the
topoisomerase I inhibitor DXd. Two analytes drive the endpoints:
**anti-HER3-ac-DXd**, the antibody-conjugated payload, and **DXd**, the released
payload. The analysis pools four Daiichi Sankyo studies -- J101 (breast cancer),
U102 and U201 (NSCLC) and U202 (colorectal cancer) -- and fits nine
endpoint-specific Bayesian models (brms / Stan): logistic regressions for
objective response and for five binary safety endpoints, and discrete-time
survival models for three time-to-event safety endpoints.

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.3674> (PMC12272309)
* Exposures came from a population PK model the paper describes only as
  "previously developed". The same group's integrated conjugate / payload model
  is packaged as `Lee_2023_patritumab`.

**No coefficient is printed anywhere in the paper or its supplement.** Every
model here is therefore a reconstruction, and the reconstruction is of two
kinds.

* **Conditional models (4)** -- ORR, grade >= 3 platelet decrease, grade >= 3
  neutrophil decrease and grade >= 3 TEAE. The paper prints typical-value
  forest plots (Figure 2, Figures S3A, S3B and S4): the predicted probability
  for a reference patient, at the 5th / 25th / 75th / 95th exposure
  percentiles, and for each influential covariate level. Those printed
  probabilities pin the intercept, the exposure slope and every covariate shift
  of the conditional model.
* **Marginal models (5)** -- SAE, grade >= 2 nausea or vomiting, ILD, AE
  leading to dose reduction and AE leading to discontinuation. Only
  population-simulated rates per dosing regimen are printed (Table 4,
  Figure 3). An intercept and an exposure slope are back-solved from the four
  fixed-dose regimens; covariates of the source model (age and Japan for SAE,
  age for dose reduction) are averaged into the intercept.

```{r models}
endpoints <- tibble::tribble(
  ~suffix,            ~endpoint,                                ~output,                          ~kind,
  "orr",              "ORR (BICR)",                             "prob_orr_central",               "conditional",
  "teae_grade3",      "Grade >= 3 TEAE",                        "prob_teae_grade3",               "conditional",
  "sae",              "SAE",                                    "prob_sae",                       "marginal",
  "plt_decrease",     "Grade >= 3 platelet count decrease",     "prob_plt_decrease",              "conditional",
  "anc_decrease",     "Grade >= 3 neutrophil count decrease",   "prob_anc_decrease",              "conditional",
  "nausea_vomiting",  "Grade >= 2 nausea or vomiting",          "prob_nausea_vomiting_grade2",    "marginal",
  "ild",              "Adjudicated drug-related ILD (6 months)", "prob_ild",                      "marginal, time-to-event",
  "dose_reduction",   "AE leading to dose reduction (6 months)", "prob_dose_reduction",           "marginal, time-to-event",
  "discontinuation",  "AE leading to discontinuation (6 months)", "prob_treatment_discontinuation", "marginal, time-to-event"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = paste0("Li_2025_patritumabDeruxtecan_", suffix))

mods <- lapply(stats::setNames(endpoints$model, endpoints$model),
               function(m) rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(m)))

# These models carry no random effects, so rxode2 warns on every
# multi-subject solve that there is no omega; only that message is muffled.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
solve_er <- function(model, events) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = events, returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = muffle_no_omega
  )
}

endpoints |>
  dplyr::select(Endpoint = endpoint, Reconstruction = kind, `Model file` = model) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "The nine models packaged from Li 2025.")
```

# Population

* **Exposure-efficacy** -- 446 patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC previously
  treated with an EGFR TKI (U102 n = 172, U201 n = 274), on 3.2-6.4 mg/kg Q3W
  or the up-titration regimen (3.2 mg/kg in Cycle 1, 4.8 mg/kg in Cycle 2,
  then 6.4 mg/kg Q3W). 29.1% had bone metastasis at baseline; 3.6% had no
  prior chemotherapy. Observed ORR 30.5%.
* **Exposure-safety** -- 715 patients from all four studies (Table S1):
  69.2% female, median age 61 years (29-83), median weight 60.0 kg
  (32.4-137); Asian 54.7%, White 37.5%, Other 5.7%, Black 2.1%; country of
  origin Japan 34.4%, other Asian 13.3%, non-Asian 52.3%; breast cancer 25.5%,
  EGFR-mutated NSCLC 62.4%, EGFR-wild-type NSCLC 6.6%, colorectal cancer 5.6%.

```{r population}
lapply(endpoints$model, function(m) {
  p <- readModelDb(m)()$population
  tibble::tibble(Model = m, N = p$n_subjects, Studies = p$n_studies)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Analysis sets, read from the packaged `population` metadata.")
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Source location |
|---|---|
| Logistic model `logit P = a + f(C) + x'g1` (binary endpoints) | Supplementary methods, display equations |
| Discrete-time survival model `logit P_ij = a0 + a_j + f(C_ij) + x'g1` | Supplementary methods, time-to-event equation |
| Log-linear exposure form `f(C) = a1 log(C)` | Supplementary methods (one of four candidate forms); chosen here because it reproduces the forest plots (below) |
| Analyte and exposure metric per endpoint | Table 2; Results ("Average anti-HER3-ac-DXd Ctrough over Cycles 1-3" for ORR) |
| Influential and significant covariates per endpoint | Table 2; Figure 2 |
| ORR: reference, exposure, titration flag, prior chemotherapy rows | Figure 2 |
| ORR: bone metastasis odds ratio 0.48 | Results, "52% (95% CrI, 1.0%, 73%) decrease in the odds" |
| Platelet decrease: all values | Figure S3A |
| Neutrophil decrease: all values | Figure S3B |
| Grade >= 3 TEAE: all values | Figure S4 |
| SAE, nausea/vomiting, ILD, dose reduction, discontinuation | Table 4 (3.2 / 4.8 / 5.6 / 6.4 mg/kg Q3W columns) |
| Reference exposures of the marginal models | Table S5, 5.6 mg/kg Q3W medians |
| Hold-out checks | Table 4 up-titration column; Results ORR text (2.25 x 77 ng/mL) |
| Population demographics | Table S1; Results, "Study populations" |
| Time-to-event endpoints evaluated at 6 months | Results ("predicted ILD rates at 6 months"); Table S7 title |

# How the coefficients were recovered

For a logistic model the printed probabilities become linear once put on the
logit scale. Each forest-plot block therefore pins a slope, and the
reference-patient row pins the intercept. The supplement lists four candidate
exposure forms (linear, log-linear, Emax and sigmoid Emax). The chunk below
refits the four exposure rows of each forest plot both ways. The log-linear form
reproduces every block at the rounding precision of the printed percentages,
and the linear form does not.

```{r form-check}
lg <- function(p) log(p / (1 - p))
forest_exposure <- tibble::tribble(
  ~endpoint,                ~C,                         ~p,
  "ORR (avg Ctrough C1-3)", c(19, 50, 132, 206),        c(20, 26, 33, 36),
  "Platelet decrease",      c(8.0, 15.5, 33.9, 58.5),   c(2.6, 6.4, 17.6, 32.9),
  "Neutrophil decrease",    c(8.0, 15.5, 33.9, 58.5),   c(3.4, 9.8, 29.1, 51.4),
  "Grade >= 3 TEAE",        c(0.6, 1.4, 3.2, 5.2),      c(28.4, 54.4, 76.9, 85.8)
)
form_check <- forest_exposure |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    loglin = max(abs(stats::resid(stats::lm(lg(p / 100) ~ log(C))))),
    linear = max(abs(stats::resid(stats::lm(lg(p / 100) ~ C))))
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
stopifnot(all(form_check$loglin < 0.025), all(form_check$linear > 0.1))
form_check |>
  dplyr::select(Endpoint = endpoint, `Log-linear` = loglin, Linear = linear) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = paste(
    "Largest logit residual of a straight-line fit to the four exposure rows",
    "of each forest plot. A 0.1 rounding step in a printed percentage near",
    "20% is about 0.006 logit."
  ))
```

Continuous covariates were fitted the same way and are linear on the logit, with
residuals of at most 0.013 logit. Categorical shifts are the logit difference
between a printed level and the reference patient. Where the forest-plot rows
imply a centring value close to a printed median (weight 60 kg, age 61 years), the
printed median is used; otherwise the implied value is used, rounded to three
significant figures.

# Check 1 -- the conditional models reproduce the forest plots

Each model is solved at the reference patient with one covariate moved to
every printed forest-plot level.

```{r forest-setup}
ref_cov <- list(
  orr = list(CTROUGH = 90.5, REGIMEN_UPTITRATION = 0, PRIOR_CHEMO = 1, BONE_MET = 0),
  plt_decrease = list(CMAX = 23.5, PLT = 243, HGB = 118, RACE_ASIAN = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0,
                      RACE_OTHER = 0, TUMTP_BREAST = 0, TUMTP_CRC = 0, TUMTP_NSCLC = 1,
                      TUM_EGFR_MUT = 1),
  anc_decrease = list(CMAX = 23.8, WT = 60, NEUT = 4.1, HGB = 118, REGION_JAPAN = 0,
                      REGION_ASIA_NONJAPAN = 0),
  teae_grade3 = list(CAV = 2.22, AGE = 61, RACE_ASIAN = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0, RACE_OTHER = 0)
)

# One row per subject; static models have no time dimension.
solve_static <- function(suffix, cov_rows) {
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(cov_rows, function(x) {
    as.data.frame(utils::modifyList(ref_cov[[suffix]], x))
  }))
  ev$id <- seq_len(nrow(ev))
  ev$time <- 0
  ev$evid <- 0L
  out <- as.data.frame(solve_er(
    mods[[paste0("Li_2025_patritumabDeruxtecan_", suffix)]], events = ev))
  out[[endpoints$output[endpoints$suffix == suffix]]]
}
```

```{r forest-check}
forest$simulated <- NA_real_
for (s in unique(forest$suffix)) {
  i <- forest$suffix == s
  forest$simulated[i] <- 100 * solve_static(s, forest$set[i])

forest <- forest |> dplyr::mutate(diff = simulated - printed)

bone <- forest$suffix == "orr" & forest$block == "Baseline bone metastasis"
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic model against its own back-solve: the only error is the
  # rounding of the printed percentages, so a tight bound is correct.
  max(abs(forest$diff[!bone])) < 0.6,
  # The bone-metastasis shift is the printed odds ratio, not the forest row.
  abs(forest$simulated[bone] - 100 * plogis(qlogis(0.30) + log(0.48))) < 1e-8
)
```

```{r forest-plot, fig.height = 9}
forest |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(endpoints, suffix, endpoint), by = "suffix") |>
  dplyr::mutate(row = paste(block, level), row = factor(row, levels = rev(unique(row)))) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = row)) +
  geom_point(aes(x = printed, shape = "Printed"), size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x = simulated, shape = "Packaged model"), size = 1.6, colour = "firebrick") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Printed = 1, `Packaged model` = 16), name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, scales = "free", ncol = 2, labeller = label_wrap_gen(30)) +
  labs(x = "Typical-value probability (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
```

Replicates Figure 2 and Figures S3A, S3B and S4 of Li 2025. Every row matches to
within `r sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(forest$diff[!bone])))` percentage points
except baseline bone metastasis. That row uses the odds ratio of 0.48 printed in the
Results, which gives `r sprintf("%.1f", forest$simulated[bone])`% against the
forest plot's 18%. A posterior-median odds ratio and a posterior-median
probability need not agree exactly.

# Check 2 -- an independent ORR statement in the text

The Results state that raising the average Cycle 1-3 trough to 2.25 times the
U201 median of 77 ng/mL "would result in a relative increase in ORR by 19.9%",
to a predicted probability of 34.3%. No part of the back-solve used this
sentence.

```{r orr-text}
p_orr <- 100 * solve_static("orr", list(list(CTROUGH = 77), list(CTROUGH = 2.25 * 77)))
orr_text <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("ORR at 2.25 x 77 ng/mL (%)", "Relative increase from 77 ng/mL (%)"),
  Printed = c(34.3, 19.9),
  Model = c(p_orr[2], 100 * (p_orr[2] / p_orr[1] - 1))
)
stopifnot(abs(orr_text$Model[1] - 34.3) < 1.5, abs(orr_text$Model[2] - 19.9) < 3)
knitr::kable(orr_text, digits = 1)
```

The small differences are expected, because the text summarises the posterior
distribution of the prediction and the forest plot summarises posterior-median
typical values.

# Check 3 -- the marginal models reproduce Table 4, including a hold-out

Each marginal model is solved at the regimen's typical exposure: the Table S5
median at 5.6 mg/kg scaled in proportion to dose. The four fixed-dose columns
were used to fit the models. The up-titration column was not, so it is a
hold-out.

* For the binary endpoints, the Cycle 1 exposure under up-titration is the
  3.2 mg/kg exposure.
* For the time-to-event endpoints, the per-cycle exposure follows the
  3.2 / 4.8 / 6.4 mg/kg steps.

The time-to-event models are solved over 6 months (182.6 days), with one
covariate record per 21-day cycle.

```{r marginal-check}
dose_fixed <- c(3.2, 4.8, 5.6, 6.4)
cref <- c(sae = 2.1, nausea_vomiting = 418, ild = 2780, dose_reduction = 24.2,
          discontinuation = 2.1)
covname <- c(sae = "CAV", nausea_vomiting = "CAV", ild = "CMAX", dose_reduction = "CMAX",
             discontinuation = "CAV")
horizon <- 182.625

solve_marginal_binary <- function(suffix, dose) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = seq_along(dose), time = 0, evid = 0L)
  ev[[covname[[suffix]]]] <- cref[[suffix]] * dose / 5.6
  out <- as.data.frame(solve_er(
    mods[[paste0("Li_2025_patritumabDeruxtecan_", suffix)]], events = ev))
  out[[endpoints$output[endpoints$suffix == suffix]]]
}

# One covariate record at the start of each 21-day cycle (LOCF), plus the
# 6-month evaluation time.
tte_events <- function(suffix, cycle_doses, id) {
  starts <- 21 * (seq_along(cycle_doses) - 1)
  ev <- data.frame(id = id, time = c(starts, horizon), evid = 0L)
  ev[[covname[[suffix]]]] <- cref[[suffix]] *
    c(cycle_doses, cycle_doses[length(cycle_doses)]) / 5.6
  ev[order(ev$time), ]
}
solve_marginal_tte <- function(suffix, regimens) {
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(regimens), function(k) {
    tte_events(suffix, regimens[[k]], k)
  }))
  out <- as.data.frame(solve_er(
    mods[[paste0("Li_2025_patritumabDeruxtecan_", suffix)]], events = ev))
  out <- out[out$time == horizon, ]
  out[[endpoints$output[endpoints$suffix == suffix]]]
}

ncyc <- ceiling(horizon / 21)
regimens <- c(lapply(dose_fixed, function(d) rep(d, ncyc)),
              list(c(3.2, 4.8, rep(6.4, ncyc - 2))))

table4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~suffix,            ~`3.2`, ~`4.8`, ~`5.6`, ~`6.4`, ~`Up-titration`,
  "sae",              28,     38,     42,     46,     28,
  "nausea_vomiting",  26,     31,     33,     35,     26,
  "ild",              2.0,    3.7,    4.7,    5.8,    5.3,
  "dose_reduction",   13,     20,     23,     26,     20,
  "discontinuation",  4.7,    7.4,    9.0,    10,     9.3
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-suffix, names_to = "regimen", values_to = "printed")

sim4 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(c("sae", "nausea_vomiting"), function(s) {
    tibble::tibble(suffix = s, regimen = c("3.2", "4.8", "5.6", "6.4", "Up-titration"),
                   simulated = 100 * solve_marginal_binary(s, c(dose_fixed, 3.2)))
  }),
  lapply(c("ild", "dose_reduction", "discontinuation"), function(s) {
    tibble::tibble(suffix = s, regimen = c("3.2", "4.8", "5.6", "6.4", "Up-titration"),
                   simulated = 100 * solve_marginal_tte(s, regimens))
  })
)
check4 <- dplyr::left_join(table4, sim4, by = c("suffix", "regimen")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = simulated - printed)

fixed_rows <- check4$regimen != "Up-titration"
holdout <- check4[!fixed_rows, ]
stopifnot(
  # Fit rows: deterministic back-solve, rounding error only.
  max(abs(check4$diff[fixed_rows])) < 0.35,
  # Hold-outs that pass: SAE and nausea/vomiting exactly, ILD and
  # discontinuation within 0.3 percentage points.
  max(abs(holdout$diff[holdout$suffix != "dose_reduction"])) < 0.3,
  # The documented dose-reduction hold-out failure (24% vs 20%).
  abs(holdout$simulated[holdout$suffix == "dose_reduction"] - 24.0) < 0.2
)

check4 |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(endpoints, suffix, endpoint), by = "suffix") |>
  dplyr::mutate(cell = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", simulated, printed)) |>
  dplyr::select(endpoint, regimen, cell) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = regimen, values_from = cell) |>
  dplyr::rename(Endpoint = endpoint, `3.2 mg/kg` = `3.2`, `4.8 mg/kg` = `4.8`,
                `5.6 mg/kg` = `5.6`, `6.4 mg/kg` = `6.4`) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Packaged marginal model (Li 2025 Table 4 in parentheses), %. The",
    "time-to-event endpoints are cumulative probabilities at 6 months. The",
    "up-titration column is a hold-out."
  ))
```

The dose-reduction hold-out fails: the model gives 24% for up-titration, where
Table 4 prints 20%. Dose reductions are front-loaded (median onset day 23,
Table S4), so the unreported cycle random effects `alpha_j` carry weight. A
constant per-cycle hazard spreads the risk evenly and so overstates it under
the high later doses of up-titration. ILD and discontinuation occur later
(median onset days 124 and 94), and their hold-outs pass.

# Figure 3 -- 5.6 mg/kg Q3W versus up-titration

Figure 3 of Li 2025 plots the 5.6 mg/kg and up-titration columns of Table 4. The
packaged models are evaluated as follows.

* The five marginal models use the dose-scaled exposures of Check 3.
* The four conditional models are evaluated at the reference patient, using the
  regimen's printed median exposure (Table S2 for ORR, Table S5 otherwise).
  For ORR, the titration flag is also set for up-titration.

```{r figure3}
typ <- tibble::tribble(
  ~suffix,         ~regimen,        ~set,
  "orr",           "5.6 mg/kg Q3W", list(CTROUGH = 90.9),
  "orr",           "Up-titration",  list(CTROUGH = 58.4, REGIMEN_UPTITRATION = 1),
  "teae_grade3",   "5.6 mg/kg Q3W", list(CAV = 2.1),
  "teae_grade3",   "Up-titration",  list(CAV = 1.1),
  "plt_decrease",  "5.6 mg/kg Q3W", list(CMAX = 24.2),
  "plt_decrease",  "Up-titration",  list(CMAX = 13.0),
  "anc_decrease",  "5.6 mg/kg Q3W", list(CMAX = 24.2),
  "anc_decrease",  "Up-titration",  list(CMAX = 13.0)
)
typ$simulated <- NA_real_
for (s in unique(typ$suffix)) {
  i <- typ$suffix == s
  typ$simulated[i] <- 100 * solve_static(s, typ$set[i])
}
fig3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::select(typ, suffix, regimen, simulated),
  check4 |>
    dplyr::filter(regimen %in% c("5.6", "Up-titration")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = ifelse(regimen == "5.6", "5.6 mg/kg Q3W", "Up-titration")) |>
    dplyr::select(suffix, regimen, simulated)
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~suffix,           ~`5.6 mg/kg Q3W`, ~`Up-titration`,
      "orr",             33,               24,
      "teae_grade3",     68,               50,
      "sae",             42,               28,
      "plt_decrease",    24,               12,
      "anc_decrease",    27,               14,
      "nausea_vomiting", 33,               26,
      "ild",             4.7,              5.3,
      "dose_reduction",  23,               20,
      "discontinuation", 9.0,              9.3
    ) |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(-suffix, names_to = "regimen", values_to = "printed"),
    by = c("suffix", "regimen")
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(endpoints, suffix, endpoint, kind), by = "suffix") |>
  dplyr::mutate(endpoint = factor(endpoint, levels = endpoints$endpoint))

ggplot(fig3, aes(x = endpoint, fill = regimen)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = simulated), position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(y = printed, group = regimen), position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
             shape = 4, size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`5.6 mg/kg Q3W` = "#1b9e77", `Up-titration` = "#d95f02"),
                    name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Endpoint probability (%)",
       caption = "Bars: packaged models. Crosses: Li 2025 Table 4 / Figure 3.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1), legend.position = "top")
```

Replicates Figure 3 of Li 2025. The marginal endpoints match by construction,
except the dose-reduction hold-out noted above. For the conditional endpoints,
the typical-value bars sit below the population-simulated crosses for the
safety endpoints, and the next section explains why. The ordering of the two
regimens is reproduced for eight of the nine endpoints. The exception is dose
reduction, where the failed hold-out places up-titration (24%) above
5.6 mg/kg (23%), while Table 4 places it below (20% vs 23%).

```{r figure3-order}
ord <- fig3 |>
  dplyr::select(suffix, regimen, simulated, printed) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = regimen, values_from = c(simulated, printed)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    same_order = sign(`simulated_5.6 mg/kg Q3W` - `simulated_Up-titration`) ==
      sign(`printed_5.6 mg/kg Q3W` - `printed_Up-titration`)
  )
stopifnot(identical(ord$suffix[!ord$same_order], "dose_reduction"))
```

# Typical value versus population average

A conditional logistic model evaluated at one typical patient is not the
average over a population. The average of `expit()` over a spread of exposures
and covariates is pulled towards 50%, and the Asian, Japanese and low-baseline
patients who dominate the NSCLC cohort sit on the high-risk side of the
reference patient. The chunk below shows the exposure part of this effect for
the platelet-decrease model. It averages the reference patient's probability
over a log-normal Cycle 1 DXd Cmax distribution, using a deterministic grid of
200 quantiles. The median is the dose-scaled Table S5 median. The log-scale SD
is 0.43, from the Table S5 5.6 mg/kg mean / median ratio,
`sqrt(2 * log(26.5 / 24.2))`.

```{r typical-vs-population}
sdlog <- sqrt(2 * log(26.5 / 24.2))
q <- (seq_len(200) - 0.5) / 200
pop <- lapply(dose_fixed, function(d) {
  cmax <- stats::qlnorm(q, meanlog = log(24.2 * d / 5.6), sdlog = sdlog)
  p <- solve_static("plt_decrease", lapply(cmax, function(x) list(CMAX = x)))
  tibble::tibble(dose = d,
                 typical = 100 * solve_static("plt_decrease", list(list(CMAX = 24.2 * d / 5.6))),
                 averaged = 100 * mean(p))
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Table 4` = c(12, 20, 24, 28))
stopifnot(all(pop$averaged > pop$typical))
pop |>
  dplyr::rename(`Dose (mg/kg Q3W)` = dose, `Typical patient, median Cmax` = typical,
                `Typical patient, averaged over Cmax` = averaged) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = paste(
    "Grade >= 3 platelet count decrease (%), reference covariates. Averaging",
    "over the exposure spread alone moves the prediction towards Table 4; the",
    "remainder is the covariate mix of the simulated NSCLC population, which",
    "the paper does not print."
  ))
```

# Exposure-response curves

```{r er-curves}
grid <- tibble::tibble(CTROUGH = exp(seq(log(3), log(400), length.out = 100)))
orr_curve <- grid |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Fixed dose` = 100 * solve_static("orr", lapply(CTROUGH, function(x) list(CTROUGH = x))),
    `Up-titration` = 100 * solve_static("orr", lapply(CTROUGH, function(x) {
      list(CTROUGH = x, REGIMEN_UPTITRATION = 1)
    }))
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-CTROUGH, names_to = "regimen", values_to = "orr")
ggplot(orr_curve, aes(CTROUGH, orr, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(19, 206), linetype = 3) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Average Cycle 1-3 anti-HER3-ac-DXd Ctrough (ng/mL)",
       y = "Typical-value ORR (%)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Dotted lines: 5th and 95th exposure percentiles (Figure 2).") +
  theme_bw()
```

Illustrates the typical-value relationship underlying Figure 1 of Li 2025 (the
figure itself is a posterior predictive check against observed response rates,
which are not reproducible without the data).

```{r tte-curves}
tte_time <- c(lapply(c(3.2, 5.6, 6.4), function(d) rep(d, 18)),
              list(c(3.2, 4.8, rep(6.4, 16))))
reg_lab <- c("3.2 mg/kg Q3W", "5.6 mg/kg Q3W", "6.4 mg/kg Q3W", "Up-titration")
curves <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("ild", "dose_reduction", "discontinuation"), function(s) {
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(tte_time), function(k) {
    starts <- 21 * (seq_along(tte_time[[k]]) - 1)
    e <- data.frame(id = k, time = sort(unique(c(starts, seq(0, 365, by = 3)))), evid = 0L)
    cyc <- pmin(floor(e$time / 21) + 1, length(tte_time[[k]]))
    e[[covname[[s]]]] <- cref[[s]] * tte_time[[k]][cyc] / 5.6
    e
  }))
  out <- as.data.frame(solve_er(mods[[paste0("Li_2025_patritumabDeruxtecan_", s)]],
                                       events = ev))
  tibble::tibble(endpoint = endpoints$endpoint[endpoints$suffix == s],
                 regimen = reg_lab[out$id], time = out$time,
                 prob = 100 * out[[endpoints$output[endpoints$suffix == s]]])
}))
ggplot(curves, aes(time, prob, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = horizon, linetype = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, scales = "free_y", labeller = label_wrap_gen(22)) +
  labs(x = "Time since first dose (days)", y = "Cumulative probability (%)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Dotted line: 6 months, the time point of Table 4.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# NCA

There is no PK in these models. Every exposure metric is an input column, so a
noncompartmental analysis would only re-measure numbers the user supplied, and
no PKNCA check is included. Users who need the exposure metrics can compute
them from the companion population PK model (`Lee_2023_patritumab`).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No coefficient is printed in the source.** All nine models are
  reconstructions. They are not the authors' posterior estimates, and each
  in-file comment names the figure or table rows the value was solved from.
* **Exposure form.** The supplement lists linear, log-linear, Emax and sigmoid
  Emax forms without saying which was chosen for each endpoint. Log-linear is
  used throughout: it reproduces all four forest plots at rounding precision,
  where the linear form does not, and it also fits the five Table 4 profiles.
* **Covariate-by-exposure interactions** (`gamma_2` in the supplement) cannot
  be identified from typical-value forest plots, which are evaluated at the
  reference exposure, and are omitted.
* **Bone metastasis** uses the odds ratio of 0.48 printed in the Results rather
  than the forest-plot row (17.1% vs 18% at the reference).
* **Reference values.**
  * Weight (60 kg) and age (61 years) are centred at the printed population
    medians.
  * The reference exposures of the conditional models and the reference
    platelets (243 x 10^9/L), neutrophils (4.1 x 10^9/L) and hemoglobin
    (118 g/L) are the values implied by the forest plots, rounded to three
    significant figures.
* **Hemoglobin unit.** Figure S3 and Table S1 label hemoglobin "g/dL", but the
  values (mean 118, range of percentiles 95-144) are g/L. The models take g/L.
* **Marginal models.**
  * SAE, nausea / vomiting, ILD, dose reduction and discontinuation are fitted
    to population-simulated rates. They assume exposure proportional to dose
    about the Table S5 5.6 mg/kg median.
  * They return population-average probabilities, and the influential
    covariates of the source (age and Japan for SAE, age for dose reduction)
    are folded into the intercept.
  * They are most faithful when given a regimen's typical exposure, not an
    individual's.
* **Time-to-event models.**
  * The cycle random effects `alpha_j ~ Normal(0, omega)` have no printed
    `omega` and are set to zero.
  * The discrete per-cycle hazard is integrated as a continuous rate over each
    21-day cycle, so survival is exact at whole-cycle boundaries and
    interpolated within a cycle.
  * Table 4 is read as 6-month cumulative probabilities, the time point the
    Results give for ILD and the title of Table S7. Six months is taken as
    182.625 days (8.7 cycles).
  * The models assume Q3W cycles; the 21-day divisor does not apply to the
    alternative Q2W regimen.
* **Dose reduction** fails its up-titration hold-out (24% vs 20%); see Check 3.
* **Residual error.** The source likelihoods are Bernoulli, with no residual
  error and no between-subject random effect. Each model carries a fixed
  placeholder additive residual SD of 0.001 on its probability output, only so
  that nlmixr2 accepts the model; it is not from the source.
* **Duration of response** was analysed only by Kaplan-Meier and log-rank test
  (Figure S1), with no model, so nothing is packaged for it.
